observations.rationale: The Approve Risk Rating activity concentrates governance density across two controls (Delegation of Authority and Rating Override Governance). Escalation routing through multi-level delegation creates serial dependency on a limited pool of senior decision-makers, extending the rating cycle time beyond target.

Rating override governance requires committee-level sign-off for any deviation from model output. The override rate metric (baseline 8%, current 14%) indicates increasing manual intervention, each instance adding 2-3 days to the approval cycle.

Data compilation relies on manual aggregation from three upstream systems. The data quality gate rejects approximately 15% of initial submissions, creating rework cycles that add 1-2 days per assessment.

Model governance check requires quarterly recalibration sign-off. Between recalibration cycles, model drift introduces estimation uncertainty. Current accuracy (88%) is below the 92% target, triggering additional manual review steps.

Risk Committee capacity is the primary throughput limiter. Committee meets bi-weekly with fixed agenda capacity, creating a batching bottleneck. Rating cycle time (baseline 10 days, current 16 days, target 8 days) confirms structural capacity constraint.

bindingConstraint.justification: The Approve Risk Rating activity is the throughput-limiting step in the Credit Risk Assessment value stream. It concentrates the highest governance density (2 controls), creates a serial dependency on Risk Committee capacity, and the rating cycle time metric confirms it as the measured bottleneck.
